headline: The package now contains the documents it tells you to read. README and SECURITY.md pointed at `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `THREAT-MODEL.md`, neither of which shipped in the tarball, and the packaging check could not see the reference because it was written as a filename rather than a link.
summary: A documentation and packaging release. No API, behavior, error, or on-disk format changes: a 2.0.1 store opens under 2.0.2 unchanged and every verb does exactly what it did. What changes is what arrives when you install the package, and whether the prose in it is accurate. Four documents that shipped docs referred to were missing from the tarball, so a reader who followed the README's own reading list found nothing; they now ship, and the packaging gate was widened so it catches a filename named in prose, not only one behind a markdown link. Widening it immediately found two more instances of the same defect. Separately, the contributor setup instructions documented a test command that fails on current Node and silently skips a chaos vector, several documents still described the store as pre-1.0 more than a year of releases later, and the architecture document's module map omitted three modules that have shipped since it was written. Every document has been rewritten for clarity, and the source comments, which ship inside the tarball and generate the API reference, are substantially shorter.

Added: `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `THREAT-MODEL.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `GOVERNANCE.md`, and `SUPPORT.md` now ship in the published package. Installing `@blamejs/stash` gives you the full document set, and every cross-reference between shipped documents resolves to a file that is actually there.
Changed: Every operator-facing document has been rewritten: the README's feature list is now a set of scannable sections rather than one unbroken block, long explanatory paragraphs are split at their topic boundaries, and dash punctuation has been restructured into ordinary sentences throughout. No documented guarantee, option, error code, or default changed wording that alters its meaning; the specification's section numbering is byte-identical, so every reference to it still resolves.

The source comments are considerably shorter. They ship inside the tarball and generate the API reference, so they are text a reader encounters. Signature restatements, repeated rationale, and narrative about how a piece of code came to be are gone; the reasoning behind each non-obvious defensive construct is kept, in shorter form.

The documentation site's sitemap no longer reports a `lastmod` date. The pages are generated when the server boots, so the only date it could compute was the current one, which restamped every URL as freshly modified on each restart. `changefreq` and `priority` are gone with it, for the same reason: they were self-reported hints with nothing behind them.
Fixed: The packaging check now verifies a document reference written as a bare filename in prose, not only one written as a markdown link. The narrower check is why the README could tell a tarball reader to open two files the tarball did not contain while the gate stayed green. Widening it found two further references to a document that was not shipping.

The contributor setup instructions documented `node --test test/` as the way to run the suite. That command fails outright on current Node versions, and where it does run it silently skips the vector that needs a forced garbage collection. The documented command is now `npm test`, which passes the flag the suite requires.

`ARCHITECTURE.md`, `THREAT-MODEL.md`, and `GOVERNANCE.md` described the store as feature-complete pre-1.0, and `SUPPORT.md` said the supported version was whatever was published most recently because the project was pre-1.0. All four now describe the shipped support policy, which is that only the current major receives fixes.
The module map in `ARCHITECTURE.md` omitted `digest.js`, `cli.js`, and `conformance.js`, three modules the same document described further down.
`LTS-CALENDAR.md` told consumers still on a `v0.x` release to upgrade to `v1.x`, a line the same document records as unserviced two sections later. It now points them at the current major.
`SECURITY.md` and `SUPPORT.md` asked reporters for a `v0.X.Y` version tag, a version series that has not been current since 1.0.
Six threat-class headings in `THREAT-MODEL.md` rendered a bold full stop after the CWE reference, and two documents broke a hyphenated word across a line so it rendered with a space after the hyphen.

The documentation site invited crawlers to index its search page, which renders a different result set for every query string and duplicates pages already in the sitemap. Search results now carry `noindex,follow`, and the page stays crawlable on purpose so that tag can be read: a `robots.txt` disallow would stop the fetch, leaving an already-indexed URL with no way to observe the removal request. The health probe answers JSON and carries no tag, so it is the one path `robots.txt` holds back. The link preview card also declared a wide image while the only image on the site is the square logo, so a share preview letterboxed it; the card type now matches the asset, and its dimensions are declared so a scraper need not fetch the file to lay the card out.
